reviews.title: Audio out of sync
reviews.text:
As other users report, the audio recorded is out of sync with the video. There is perhaps a half second delay, so you see the lips stop moving about a half second before the audio stops. It’s very distracting watching the final output. While recording, the prompt speed is supposed to move at the pace the presenter is speaking, but it frequently stops moving at all. 
I’ll try it for a bit longer to see if there are conditions under which it functions as advertised, but at present it appears that it is not fit for purpose. Nice idea, badly implemented.

It’s perfectly awful in terms of ease of use. Surely there must be a means by which one can simply cut and paste from ordinary sources? I just want to cut, paste, read, and record. It’s not working for me in terms of workflow.

reviews.title: The Korean font is not supported, and the speed is too fast!
reviews.text: I’ve been using it for several years. I don‘t know what kind of version has been up for a few years. Korean fonts are still not supported, and all the sentences copied from Google Drive look like a strange format, and above all, the speed starts from 70, which is too fast for those who are slow to speak or have language disabilities. In fact, if ordinary people put it at 70, they are all too fast, so they have to adjust it by attaching one person to the side with a remote app. And even if I ask for help, there is no answer. It’s my final conclusion that it‘s not an app to pay for.

reviews.title: Recordings are unusable - audio drifts out of sync
reviews.text:
The teleprompter side of this app works well. VoiceTrack is genuinely clever. The problem is the recording function, which is the whole reason to use it.
Videos recorded in the app have audio that drifts progressively out of sync. It's not a fixed delay you can correct in an editor - the drift gets worse across the recording, so nothing lines up no matter how you shift it. The cause is that the app records video at a variable frame rate while the audio stays constant. Editing software assumes a constant frame rate, so every recording comes out looking badly dubbed.
I found this out after filming videos I couldn't afford to reshoot, then spent an afternoon diagnosing the files and repairing them with command line tools. Most people won't have the technical background to do that, and shouldn't need to. They'll just have ruined footage.
Until the developer fixes the recording pipeline to output constant frame rate video, I'd avoid recording in this app entirely. Use it as a prompter with a separate camera if you must, but that defeats the point of buying it.

reviews.title: Weekly user. It’s… ugh. Fine.
reviews.text:
Does what I need, but the price is so aggravating for the glitches I face. 

Super expensive for what it is. I had a 3* and just switched to 2*

What’s GOOD:
It follows my voice. That is why I bought the app. 

What’s BAD:
1) subscriptions. Hate renewing. Hate the price. 

2) formatting. 
A) Sometimes I wish the words went bigger than size 10 so I could view when recording from farther back 
B) copy/paste often includes black text, but not always. Not until I get into recording the script does it just disappear my text. (Dark text on dark background instead of white text on dark background.)
C) not easy to import. Formatting is whacky
D) I eventually just CLEAR the formatting which removes key words I wanted to emphasize with bold, etc. 
E) still no clue why there are so many title fields. The layers of scripts are so weird. No clue why it’s laid out like it is. 

3) login. Never saves login. Have to log in every time. Not the highest security risk platform. People can get my scripts, it’s fine. I hate logging in every single time. And it always puts the login page behind a couple of clicks. 

Overall not a fan. If I find something better, I’m out.

reviews.title: More bugs than a roach motel
reviews.text: I bought this app to narrate a documentary in Malaysia. I tested it briefly on my iPhone 17 Pro Max before leaving, and it appeared fine. However, once on location, the app struggled to switch the dialogue box to landscape, froze multiple times, and crashed repeatedly. My main issue was that the voice-activated scrolling didn't work at all. I tried using the iPhone’s built-in mic and a DJI Mic 2 paired with the phone, but the script either would scroll just one line before freezing or wouldn't start altogether. I performed several hard and soft resets of the phone, but nothing helped. In all, it was a complete failure and set back our production while I found another teleprompter app that did work.
